newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses surge, Frankfurt ends at record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses surge, Frankfurt ends at record.

text.p: European bourses climbed sharply on Friday with Frankfurt propelled to a record close by the stronger dollar boosting prospects for German exporters.
Paris stocks surged to their highest level of the year as investors hoped for a speedy end to the French truckers' strike and drew comfort from the dollar's gains and higher bond prices.
On currency markets the dollar rose against the mark as traders fretted about growing tension between France and Germany over exchange rates and monetary policy.
In Frankfurt, shares ended a record-breaking week by closing at an all-time high of 2845.52 points on the DAX index, up 28.03 points, and making a gain of three percent in just one week.
"The dynamism of the current climb had been surprising," said Peter Pietsch, economist at Germany's Commerzbank.

Market analysts, who had widely forecast a year-end level of 2,850 points, said the DAX could now charge ahead to 2,900 points by the end of the year. Some said the once-unthinkable 3,000 point level now seemed within the grasp of the market.

The market was driven by a dream combination of strength in German government bonds, which have reached all-time highs, and the stronger dollar, benefiting German exporting sectors, in particular the chemical industry.

In Paris, stocks roared ahead one one stage by 1.4 percent to 2327.81 on the blue-chip CAC-40, eclipsing the previous intra-day high for 1996 of 2,295.54 and edging closer to its record of 2360.98 set in Ferbruary 1994.
"The bourse is feeling very bullish," a trader said, amid signs of optimism over the 12-day-old truckers' dispute.
The strike by drivers blockading the country neared conclusion on Friday after unions signed an early retirement deal and consulted their members at roadblocks on ending the action.

The sparkling performances in Paris and Frankfurt was largely thanks to the strengthening dollar. It was lifted again by Bank of France monetary policy council member Jean-Pierre Gerard when he said on Thursday he favoured a stronger dollar against the mark.
One way to drive the dollar higher would be to tempt dollar investors by cutting short-term rates in France and Germany, making equities more attractive.
In London, suffering from stronger sterling, shares climbed cautiously higher after Thursday's late rally sparked by renewed bid speculation.

But a healthy opening on Wall Street, up 0.4 percent, encouraged the market in mid-afternoon and some traders said London's FTSE index, which on Tuesday touched a record intraday high, could stil go for its traditional year-end rally.

"My feeling is this market wants to go better," said the head of sales trading at one brokerage. "The market is nervous but with fund managers holding plenty of cash, the likelihood is it will respond more aggressively to good news rather than bad."
The dollar climbed half a pfennig to 1.5380 marks after Gerard joined the growing French chorus in support of a stronger dollar.

"In a sense France is holding a loaded gun to Germany's head saying either we revalue mark/Paris or Europe as a block devalues against the U.S. and the rest of the world," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"What we are seeing is a questioning of the central plank of French macroeconomic policy of the last 10 years. It's a very fundamental issue," he added.
"In the short term, the dollar will continue to derive some encouragement from this uncertainty about European exchange-rate policy," he said.
The pound soared to a 33-month peak against the mark as a rise in British interest rate looked increasingly likely to staunch inflationary pressures. It was at 2.5821 marks and $1.6845 at one point.
CURRENCIES at 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.82 yen and 1.5380 marks against 113.61 yen and 1.5320 marks in late Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 12.3 points at 4,062.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 26.48 at 2,316.79.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 28.03 at 2845.52.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $371.30 an ounce in the afternoon, compared with $372.70 at the London close on Thursday. Silver was unchanged at $4.74.
